rationale: Queuing a probe for the store-breadth point that the parent account still lists as a limitation: the same single-node history is written into a commit-tracking store that is also marked monotonic, the store reports the entries as committed, and the node is constructed from it with RestoreCommittedLogs. Local construction feedback shows the recovered configuration empty with the applied index at the staged commit index, so the gap appears with that store shape as well; the retained receipt is what the account will rest on.

scope.description: A single-node history is written directly into a commit-tracking store that also reports itself as monotonic: a configuration entry at index 1, ten command entries above it, and a staged commit index covering them, with the stable store holding term one. NewRaft is then run against that store with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and snapshotting disabled, and the probe reports the store's monotonicity, the last log index, the staged commit index, the applied index, and the node's configuration after construction.
assumptions: The store is the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore wrapped by a harness type whose IsMonotonic reports true; the stable store, transport, FSM and snapshot store are the repository's own in-memory facilities.
The history is the same one a bootstrapped single-node cluster writes: a configuration entry at index 1 followed by commands, with the commit index staged as the entries are stored.
No snapshot exists, so the recovered configuration can only come from the scan or from nothing.

experiment.prefix: Create the monotonic commit-tracking store and an in-memory stable store; store a configuration entry at index 1 for a single voter named self, then ten command entries at indexes 2 to 11; stage commit index eleven; set the stable store's current term to one; build a DefaultConfig with LocalID self, RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, a very large snapshot threshold and a one-hour snapshot interval; construct the node with NewRaft over an in-memory transport and snapshot store; emit the resulting store monotonicity, last log index, staged commit index, applied index and the node's configuration.
experiment.requirement: A node constructed from a store that reports a configuration entry as committed must hold the configuration that entry records, whatever shape the store has.
experiment.responsibility: Raft itself: NewRaft decides how the recovered configuration is established, independently of the store implementation.
